question: What is HTML and what is it used for?
key_points: Markup language for structuring web page content
Uses elements/tags such as headings, paragraphs, links, images
Browser reads HTML to display the page

question: What is the difference between HTML, CSS and JavaScript?
key_points: HTML gives structure/content
CSS gives styling and layout
JavaScript adds behaviour and interactivity

question: What is the difference between block and inline elements in HTML?
key_points: Block elements start on a new line and take full width (div, p)
Inline elements stay in the line and take only needed width (span, a)
Width/height mostly apply to block elements

question: What are semantic HTML tags? Give two examples.
key_points: Tags that describe the meaning of content
Examples: header, nav, main, article, footer, section
Help accessibility and SEO

question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute on an image?
key_points: Text alternative describing the image
Read by screen readers for accessibility
Shown if the image fails to load

question: What are the three ways to add CSS to a web page?
key_points: Inline style attribute
Internal style tag in the head
External .css file linked with link tag

question: What is the CSS box model?
key_points: Content, padding, border and margin
Padding is inside the border, margin outside
Determines total size and spacing of an element

question: What is the difference between a class and an id selector in CSS?
key_points: Class selector uses a dot and can be reused on many elements
Id selector uses # and should be unique on the page
Id has higher specificity than class

question: What is the difference between margin and padding?
key_points: Padding is space inside the border around content
Margin is space outside the border between elements
Background colour covers padding but not margin

question: What is a responsive website?
key_points: Layout adapts to different screen sizes
Uses flexible layouts, relative units and media queries
Works well on mobile, tablet and desktop

question: What is a media query in CSS?
key_points: Applies CSS rules only when a condition is true
Usually based on screen width, e.g. @media (max-width: 600px)
Used to build responsive designs

question: What is Flexbox used for?
key_points: One-dimensional CSS layout (row or column)
Aligns and distributes space between items
Uses properties like justify-content and align-items

question: What is the difference between let, const and var in JavaScript?
key_points: var is function-scoped, let and const are block-scoped
const cannot be reassigned, let can
var is hoisted and initialised as undefined

question: What are the primitive data types in JavaScript?
key_points: string, number, boolean
undefined, null
bigint and symbol

question: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
key_points: == compares values after type conversion
=== compares value and type without conversion
=== is preferred to avoid unexpected results

question: What is a function in JavaScript?
key_points: Reusable block of code that performs a task
Can take parameters and return a value
Defined with function keyword or arrow syntax

question: What is an arrow function?
key_points: Shorter syntax for writing functions using =>
Does not have its own this; uses this of the surrounding scope
Commonly used for callbacks

question: What is an array and how do you add an item to it in JavaScript?
key_points: Ordered list of values accessed by index starting at 0
push adds to the end, unshift adds to the start
Arrays can hold mixed types

question: What is an object in JavaScript?
key_points: Collection of key-value pairs (properties)
Values can be data or functions (methods)
Accessed with dot or bracket notation

question: What is the DOM?
key_points: Document Object Model: tree representation of the HTML page
JavaScript uses it to read and change elements
Changes to the DOM update what the user sees

question: How do you select an element by its id in JavaScript?
key_points: document.getElementById('id')
or document.querySelector('#id')
Returns the element or null if not found

question: What is an event listener?
key_points: Function that runs when an event happens on an element
Added with addEventListener, e.g. 'click'
Used to make pages interactive

question: What is React?
key_points: JavaScript library for building user interfaces
UI is built from reusable components
Uses a virtual DOM to update the page efficiently

question: What is a component in React?
key_points: Reusable, independent piece of UI
Usually a function that returns JSX
Can receive props and keep its own state

question: What is JSX?
key_points: Syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like code in JavaScript
Compiled to React.createElement calls
Uses className instead of class

question: What are props in React?
key_points: Inputs passed from a parent to a child component
Read-only inside the child
Used to make components reusable

question: What is state in React?
key_points: Data that a component manages and that can change
Updating state re-renders the component
In function components managed with useState

question: What is Git and why do developers use it?
key_points: Distributed version control system
Tracks changes and history of code
Lets teams work together using branches and merges

question: What is the difference between git commit and git push?
key_points: commit saves changes to the local repository
push uploads local commits to the remote repository
Commits can be made offline; push needs the remote

question: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
key_points: HTTPS is HTTP encrypted with TLS/SSL
Protects data from being read or changed in transit
Browsers show a lock icon for HTTPS

question: Explain CSS specificity with an example.
key_points: Decides which rule wins when rules conflict
Order: inline > id > class/attribute/pseudo-class > element
!important overrides normal specificity; later rule wins on a tie

question: What is the difference between position relative, absolute and fixed?
key_points: relative moves an element from its normal position
absolute positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor
fixed positions relative to the viewport and stays on scroll

question: When would you use CSS Grid instead of Flexbox?
key_points: Grid is two-dimensional (rows and columns)
Flexbox is one-dimensional
Grid suits full page or card layouts; Flexbox suits aligning items in a row/column

question: What is the difference between display none and visibility hidden?
key_points: display:none removes the element from layout
visibility:hidden hides it but keeps its space
Both hide content from view

question: What does mobile-first design mean?
key_points: Design and write CSS for small screens first
Add styles for larger screens with min-width media queries
Keeps mobile layout simple and fast

question: What is hoisting in JavaScript?
key_points: Declarations are moved to the top of their scope before execution
var is hoisted as undefined; function declarations are fully hoisted
let/const are hoisted but in the temporal dead zone until declared

question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
key_points: A function that remembers variables from its outer scope
Works even after the outer function has returned
Used for data privacy and function factories

question: Explain the difference between map, filter and reduce.
key_points: map transforms each item and returns a new array of same length
filter returns items that pass a condition
reduce combines items into a single value

question: What is the difference between null and undefined?
key_points: undefined: variable declared but not assigned
null: intentional empty value set by the programmer
typeof null is 'object', typeof undefined is 'undefined'

question: What is a Promise in JavaScript?
key_points: Object representing a future result of an async operation
States: pending, fulfilled, rejected
Handled with then/catch or async/await

question: How does async/await work?
key_points: async function always returns a Promise
await pauses inside the function until the Promise settles
Errors are handled with try/catch

question: What is the event loop in JavaScript?
key_points: JavaScript runs on a single thread with a call stack
Async callbacks wait in queues (microtask, task)
Event loop moves them to the stack when it is empty

question: What does the spread operator do?
key_points: ... expands an array or object into individual elements
Used to copy or merge arrays/objects
Creates a shallow copy

question: What is destructuring in JavaScript?
key_points: Extracting values from arrays or objects into variables
const {name} = user; const [a, b] = arr
Supports default values and renaming

question: What is event bubbling?
key_points: Event triggers on the target then moves up through its ancestors
stopPropagation stops it from bubbling
Allows event delegation on a parent element

question: What is event delegation?
key_points: Attach one listener to a parent instead of many children
Use event.target to find which child was clicked
Works for elements added later and saves memory

question: What is the difference between localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies?
key_points: localStorage persists until cleared; sessionStorage ends with the tab
Cookies are sent with every HTTP request and can expire
Cookies are small (~4KB); storage holds more (~5MB)

question: How do you make an API call from the browser?
key_points: Use fetch (or a library like axios) with a URL
Handle the returned Promise with then or async/await
Parse JSON response and handle errors

question: What is the virtual DOM in React?
key_points: Lightweight copy of the real DOM kept in memory
React compares old and new virtual DOM (diffing)
Only changed parts are updated in the real DOM

question: Explain the useEffect hook.
key_points: Runs side effects after render (API calls, subscriptions)
Dependency array controls when it re-runs
Return function is used for cleanup

question: Why do we need keys when rendering lists in React?
key_points: Keys help React identify which items changed, added or removed
Should be unique and stable, e.g. an id
Using index as key can cause bugs when list order changes

question: What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components?
key_points: Controlled: input value stored in React state and updated via onChange
Uncontrolled: DOM keeps the value, read with a ref
Controlled inputs make validation easier

question: What is lifting state up in React?
key_points: Moving shared state to the closest common parent
Parent passes state and setter as props to children
Keeps sibling components in sync

question: What is prop drilling and how can you avoid it?
key_points: Passing props through many levels that do not use them
Avoid with Context API
Or a state library such as Redux/Zustand

question: What is the Context API in React?
key_points: Shares data across components without passing props
createContext, Provider and useContext
Good for theme, auth user, language

question: How does routing work in a React or Next.js app?
key_points: Maps URLs to components/pages
React Router uses Route components; Next.js uses file-based routing
Navigation happens without full page reload

question: What is the difference between client-side and server-side rendering?
key_points: CSR: browser downloads JS and builds the page
SSR: server sends ready HTML for each request
SSR helps first load speed and SEO

question: What is web accessibility and how can you improve it?
key_points: Making sites usable for people with disabilities
Semantic HTML, alt text, labels, keyboard navigation
Good colour contrast and ARIA where needed

question: How can you improve the loading speed of a web page?
key_points: Compress and lazy-load images
Minify and bundle CSS/JS, code splitting
Use caching and a CDN

question: What is CORS?
key_points: Browser security rule for requests to a different origin
Server must allow the origin with Access-Control-Allow-Origin header
Otherwise the browser blocks the response

question: What is a REST API from a frontend developer's view?
key_points: Backend exposes resources at URLs
Frontend uses HTTP methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
Data is usually exchanged as JSON

question: What do HTTP status codes 200, 404 and 500 mean?
key_points: 200 OK: request succeeded
404 Not Found: resource does not exist
500 Internal Server Error: problem on the server

question: What is a merge conflict in Git and how do you resolve it?
key_points: Happens when two branches change the same lines
Git marks the conflict in the file
Edit to keep the correct code, then add and commit

question: What is the difference between git merge and git rebase?
key_points: merge combines branches with a merge commit and keeps history
rebase moves commits on top of another branch for linear history
Do not rebase shared/public branches

question: What is a pull request?
key_points: Request to merge a branch into another, e.g. into main
Teammates review the code and comment
Checks/tests can run before merging

question: Why is code review useful?
key_points: Finds bugs early
Improves code quality and consistency
Shares knowledge within the team

question: What is XSS (cross-site scripting)?
key_points: Attacker injects malicious script into a web page
Script runs in other users' browsers and can steal data
Prevent by escaping output and not using innerHTML with user input

question: Where should a frontend store an authentication token?
key_points: httpOnly cookie protects the token from JavaScript (XSS)
localStorage is simple but readable by any script
Use HTTPS and short expiry

question: Why should you never put secret keys in frontend code?
key_points: Frontend code is downloaded and readable by anyone
Keys can be stolen and misused
Keep secrets on the server and use environment variables there

question: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code?
key_points: Synchronous runs line by line and blocks
Asynchronous starts a task and continues without waiting
Results handled with callbacks, Promises or async/await

question: A React component re-renders too often. How would you find and fix the cause?
key_points: Use React DevTools Profiler to see what re-renders
Check changing props/state and new object/function props each render
Fix with React.memo, useMemo/useCallback or moving state down

question: Explain useMemo and useCallback and when not to use them.
key_points: useMemo caches a computed value; useCallback caches a function
Both depend on a dependency array
Overusing adds complexity; use only for expensive work or stable references

question: What happens when you type a URL in the browser and press Enter?
key_points: DNS lookup finds the server IP
TCP/TLS connection and HTTP request
Server responds with HTML; browser parses, loads CSS/JS and renders the page

question: Your useEffect calls an API in an infinite loop. Why and how do you fix it?
key_points: Effect updates state that is also in its dependency array
Or a new object/function is created every render
Fix the dependency array or memoise values; add cleanup

question: How would you design a reusable form with validation in React?
key_points: Controlled inputs with state for values and errors
Validate on change/submit and show messages
Can use a library like React Hook Form with a schema (Zod/Yup)

question: How does the browser render a page, and what is a reflow?
key_points: Builds DOM and CSSOM, combines into render tree
Layout (reflow) calculates positions, then paint
Changing size/position triggers reflow, which is costly

question: How would you implement infinite scrolling in a React list?
key_points: Detect when the user is near the bottom (IntersectionObserver)
Fetch the next page and append items
Handle loading state, end of data and avoid duplicate requests

question: What is debouncing and where would you use it?
key_points: Delays a function until the user stops triggering it for a set time
Used for search input and resize events
Reduces unnecessary API calls

question: Predict the output: for (var i=0;i<3;i++) setTimeout(()=>console.log(i),0). Why?
key_points: Prints 3, 3, 3
var is function-scoped so all callbacks share one i
Using let creates a new i per iteration and prints 0, 1, 2

question: How do Promise.all and Promise.allSettled differ?
key_points: Promise.all rejects as soon as one promise rejects
Promise.allSettled waits for all and returns each result status
Use allSettled when partial failures are acceptable

question: What is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy of an object?
key_points: Shallow copy copies top-level properties; nested objects are shared
Deep copy duplicates nested objects too
Use structuredClone or careful recursion for deep copy

question: How does the this keyword behave in different JavaScript functions?
key_points: In a method, this is the object calling it
In a regular function it is undefined in strict mode (or global)
Arrow functions take this from the surrounding scope; bind/call/apply set it

question: How would you manage global state in a large React app?
key_points: Keep local state local and lift only what is shared
Context for small global data; Redux/Zustand for complex state
Use a data-fetching library (React Query) for server state

question: How would you make a slow page with many images load faster?
key_points: Lazy-load images below the fold
Serve compressed modern formats and correct sizes
Use a CDN, caching and placeholders

question: How would you handle errors from API calls in a React app?
key_points: Use try/catch or .catch and check response status
Show user-friendly messages and loading states
Error boundaries for render errors; retry where sensible

question: How would you protect a frontend app against XSS and CSRF?
key_points: Escape/sanitise user content; avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML
Content Security Policy
For CSRF: SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens

question: How would you implement protected routes in a React app?
key_points: Check if the user is logged in (token/session) before rendering
Redirect to login if not authenticated
Server must still verify the token on every API call

question: How would you structure folders in a medium-sized React project?
key_points: Group by feature or by type (components, hooks, services)
Keep reusable UI components separate
Central API layer and consistent naming

question: What is code splitting and why is it useful?
key_points: Splits the JS bundle into smaller chunks
Loads code only when needed (React.lazy, dynamic import)
Reduces initial load time

question: How would you test a React component?
key_points: Unit test with Jest and React Testing Library
Test behaviour: render, user events, expected output
Mock API calls; add end-to-end tests with Cypress/Playwright

question: What is a backend in a web application?
key_points: Server-side part of the application
Handles business logic, database and authentication
Exposes APIs that the frontend calls

question: What is an API?
key_points: Application Programming Interface
Set of rules for how programs communicate
Web APIs expose endpoints over HTTP

question: What is a REST API?
key_points: API style using HTTP and resources identified by URLs
Uses methods GET, POST, PUT/PATCH, DELETE
Stateless; usually exchanges JSON

question: What are the main HTTP methods and their uses?
key_points: GET reads data
POST creates data
PUT/PATCH updates, DELETE removes

question: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
key_points: PUT replaces the whole resource
PATCH updates only some fields
Both are used for updates

question: What do status codes 200, 201, 400, 401 and 404 mean?
key_points: 200 OK, 201 Created
400 Bad Request (invalid input), 401 Unauthorized (not logged in)
404 Not Found

question: What is JSON?

Key-value pairs and arrays
Common format for API requests and responses

question: What is Node.js?

Built on Chrome's V8 engine
Non-blocking, event-driven; good for APIs

question: What is Express.js?

Handles routing and middleware
